title: Quest Acceptance vs Completion Ratio
dataSources: Life score (`lifeos:score`), quests / tasks (`quest:task`), habit streaks (`streak:status`), life achievements (`achievement:life`), household leaderboard (`household:leaderboard`), plus every other `index=personal` sourcetype as input.
app: The parody-the-enterprise meta layer — a Personal NOC (house-health wall), Personal SOC (entry / impossible-travel), Personal SRE (SLOs on your own habits), and a gamification layer (XP, achievements, streaks, household leaderboards) — all computed in Splunk over `index=personal`.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=quest:task
| stats sum(eval(if(status="accepted",1,0))) as accepted, sum(eval(if(status="done",1,0))) as completed by quest_board
| eval completion_pct=round(100*completed/accepted,1)
| sort - completion_pct
description: Compares how many quests you take on with how many you actually finish in each quest board.
value: Overaccepting goals is a classic productivity failure mode, and this ratio makes it obvious.
implementation: Use quest status in `quest:task` and calculate board-level completion percentage from accepted to done.
visualization: Table of quest boards with acceptance versus completion.
grandmaExplanation: It watches whether you are taking on more quests than you really finish.
